          UEFA Women’s Champions League: Opta Supercomputer Matchday 3 Predictions
        
      
                          
                      Oct 28, 2026
          
                      Emily Clogg / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
With the help of the Opta supercomputer, we provide our UEFA Women’s Champions League match predictions for Matchday 3.
Matchday 3 of the 2026-27 UEFA Women’s Champions League is upon us and after what has been an almost month-long wait, the anticipation has built ahead of another week of fixtures.

With two wins from their opening two matches, Barcelona are the only side to have maintained a perfect start to the competition. Pere Romeu’s side put six past Roma last time out as Caroline Graham Hansen, Clàudia Pina and Ewa Pajor all found the net.

For all three English sides in the competitions, things weren’t quite so straightforward. Chelsea, Manchester City and Arsenal all drew their clashes with OL Lyonnes, Real Madrid and Paris FC respectively.
For the latter, it was a moment of sheer madness from Leah Williamson that turned three valuable points to just one in the French capital; elsewhere in the city, PSG thrashed OH Leuven 5-0.

This week’s set of fixtures features a number of delectable matchups. The two standouts see Bayern Munich host Real Madrid on Wednesday, before Manchester City face PSG at the Joie Stadium the next day.
Elsewhere, Chelsea host Roma, Arsenal welcome Benfica, and Barcelona head to Denmark to take on HB Køge.
Here, we look out the Opta supercomputer's data-led predictions for each game on MD3.
There are three 17:45 (GMT) kick-offs to choose from on Wednesday, one of which is guaranteed to be an entertaining affair as Real Madrid make the trip to Germany to take on Bayern Munich.

In this early stage of the UWCL, there are few trickier tasks than beating Bayern in front of their own fans. In fact, José Barcala’s side haven’t lost a single round-one match at home (W12 D4); only Barcelona and Chelsea have played as many such matches without defeat.

As for Real Madrid, they’ve lost just one of their last eight league-phase matches (2-1 defeat to Arsenal last term), with their last three all ending in a draw, the longest such streak in the competition alongside PSG.
This is the first UWCL meeting between the two sides, and the supercomputer expects a one-way encounter with Bayern winning 60.6% % of pre-match simulations.

Meanwhile, Sonia Bompastor’s Chelsea welcome Roma to the English capital, with the Blues boasting an enviable record against Italian sides in the competition; they are unbeaten across their previous five (W4 D1).
The Blues enter this one with a spring in their step, having leapfrogged City to the summit of the Women’s Super League table at the weekend following a 3-1 win against promoted side Crystal Palace.
Roma are also top of their respective domestic table, the Serie A Femminile, but have been struggling in Europe, and enter this fixture looking for their first win of the new campaign.

Yet to score a goal, Roma are the only team to have underperformed by 2+ goals based on the xG they’ve generated in this season’s UWCL (-2.53). However, Chelsea are also just  one of four others to have underperformed by at least one goal (-1.17).
The Blues are strong favourites going into this match-up, and the pre-match sims saw them take all three points 81.2% of the time.
Wednesday's other early kick-off is a crucial clash as Servette host OH Leuven, with both teams looking to kick-start their Champions League campaigns. Neither side has scored a goal yet.
The supercomputer leans slightly towards a first win in the competition for Servette, who came out on top in 47.3% of simulations.
Wednesday's 20:00 (GMT) matches feature two European heavyweights, with Lyon and Arsenal both in action hosting Inter and Benfica, respectively.
